chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, saying: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Isbahani, from Al-Sulayman ibn Dawud Al-Manquri, from Sufyan 'Aynah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

I found the knowledge of all people to be contained in four things: the first is to know your Lord, the second is to know what He has done for you, the third is to know what He wants from you, and the fourth is to know what will take you out of your religion.

key_terms.أَرَادَ مِنْكَ: What He wants from you (divine will/command)
key_terms.صَنَعَ بِكَ: What He has done for you (blessings/grace)
key_terms.يُخْرِجُكَ مِنْ دِينِكَ: What takes you out of your religion (causes of apostasy/error)

ai.seo_question: What are the four essential components of knowledge according to Imam Al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) defining the totality of religious knowledge (*'ilm*) through a fourfold epistemological framework: recognizing the Creator, acknowledging His blessings, discerning His will, and identifying the markers of apostasy. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on *ma'rifah* (gnosis) as a holistic state that integrates theological certainty with practical self-awareness and vigilance against spiritual deviation.
